technologies.name: Energy audits
technologies.benefit: Reveals each neighbourhood's biggest energy losses. Unlocks rooftop solar and deeper retrofit research.
technologies.limit: Cheap and fast, but the savings depend on the building and on people acting on the findings.

technologies.name: Building retrofits
technologies.benefit: Insulation and windows cut heating demand and raise comfort.
technologies.limit: Strong in older, poorly insulated housing; deep retrofits are costly and disruptive.

technologies.name: Heat pumps
technologies.benefit: Move heat rather than burn fuel, so homes get several units of heat per unit of electricity.
technologies.limit: Efficient heat, but less so in very cold weather; works best in homes that are retrofitted first.

technologies.name: Energy cooperatives
technologies.benefit: Residents jointly own local renewable energy: more clean power and a stronger sense of ownership.
technologies.limit: Many European communities run them, but success depends on local rules and steady organising effort.

technologies.name: Community gardens and allotments
technologies.benefit: Shared food growing: food, green space and engagement in a neighbourhood.
technologies.limit: Meaningful social benefits, but only a small share of a town's total food.

technologies.name: Composting
technologies.benefit: Diverts food waste and builds soil fertility for nearby gardens.
technologies.limit: Needs good sorting and careful management of smells and pests.

technologies.name: Local food hubs and markets
technologies.benefit: A weekly market brings local growers and residents together: more local food, less packaging.
technologies.limit: Shorter chains help local growers, but local does not always mean lower emissions.

technologies.name: Safe walking and cycling streets
technologies.benefit: Walking and cycling infrastructure: mobility up, car emissions down.
technologies.limit: Works best as a connected network, not isolated lanes.

technologies.name: Frequent public transport
technologies.benefit: Unlocks bus lines between neighbouring neighbourhoods (they cross the river only at the bridges).
technologies.limit: Frequency and reliability matter more than coverage; low-density areas are harder to serve.

technologies.name: Shared mobility (car and bike sharing)
technologies.benefit: Shared bikes and cars mean fewer cars per household and easier trips without owning one.
technologies.limit: Helps most where density and good alternatives already exist.

technologies.name: Repair cafés and tool libraries
technologies.benefit: Neighbours fix and share things instead of throwing them away: less waste, more engagement.
technologies.limit: Repair sits above recycling in the waste hierarchy, but needs volunteers and a space to meet.

technologies.name: Separate collection and recycling
technologies.benefit: Sorted collection points raise the share of waste that is recycled.
technologies.limit: Quality depends on clean sorting, and recycling is not the same as preventing waste.

technologies.name: Pollinator meadows
technologies.benefit: Mowing less and sowing native flowers turns lawns into green space that is alive with insects.
technologies.limit: Benefits grow over several seasons, and a tidy-lawn culture can resist the change.

technologies.name: Urban trees and green roofs
technologies.benefit: Street trees add shade, cooling and green space that residents notice every day.
technologies.limit: Young trees need water and care for years; green roofs need structural support.

technologies.name: Rain gardens and wetlands
technologies.benefit: Planted hollows and wetlands soak up and filter runoff along the river.
technologies.limit: They need space and upkeep, and cannot stop extreme floods on their own.

technologies.name: Community learning
technologies.benefit: Evening workshops at the school or library: residents learn together and the town gains Knowledge each month.
technologies.limit: Turnout depends on timing and childcare; the same keen people often come every time.
